title: BCCI Informs Rohit Sharma He Is No Longer in India's ODI Plans Beyond England Series

body:
India's cricket establishment is preparing to move on from one of its greatest white-ball players. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has informed veteran opener Rohit Sharma that he is no longer part of the selectors' long-term plans in ODI cricket, according to multiple reports.

## Selectors Push for Youth Ahead of 2027 World Cup

The BCCI's senior selection committee, along with head coach Gautam Gambhir, held discussions with Rohit last week and conveyed the team's roadmap going forward, The Indian Express reported. With the third and final ODI against England set for Lord's on July 19, it could potentially be Rohit's farewell appearance in the 50-over format.

"Selectors have informed Rohit he is not in their scheme of things post the England tour and they are moving on from him after this series. Though he wanted to continue, especially after working on his fitness. The selectors have left the ball in Sharma's court to decide his future," a source told The Indian Express.

The 39-year-old has struggled for runs in the ongoing ODI series against England, managing just 11 in the first ODI at Edgbaston and 26 off 47 deliveries in the second ODI at Sophia Gardens in Cardiff on July 16. His combined tally of 37 runs across two matches has intensified scrutiny.

## Divided Opinions Within the Setup

Reports suggest the decision has created a rift within the selection committee. While chief selector Ajit Agarkar and head coach Gambhir favour investing in younger players — with Yashasvi Jaiswal expected to get more opportunities — two other selectors, Pragyan Ojha and RP Singh, are reportedly backing Rohit due to his vast experience and recent form in ICC tournaments.

Captain Shubman Gill has also expressed support for keeping both Rohit and Virat Kohli in the squad, according to CricketAddictor.

## What It Means for Diaspora Cricket Fans

For millions of Indian cricket fans around the world who have watched Rohit's career spanning over 15 years, the potential end of his ODI journey is significant. Rohit led India to back-to-back ICC titles — the T20 World Cup in 2024 and the Champions Trophy in 2025 — cementing his legacy as one of India's most successful captains.

His childhood coach Dinesh Lad remains confident: "I don't think Rohit is insecure. He is hundred per cent eligible for World Cup," he told MyKhel.

The series decider at Lord's on July 19 could offer Rohit Sharma one final chapter on English soil — and Indian fans across the globe will be watching.
